findings.title: No verified end-to-end production dry run since the identity and provisioning overhaul
findings.evidence: CLIENT_READINESS.md section H (H1-H18) is unchecked; ROADMAP.md Phase 2 row 32 records a dry run completed 2026-06-01. Since then the auth/provisioning stack was rebuilt: portal named-user cutover (apps/portal/lib/session.ts isProdLikeEnv fail-closed gate; ROADMAP 'PR B'/'PR C' marked in progress), credential authority (api/credential_authority.py with production bugs fixed during 'live incident recovery', ROADMAP Platform Recovery R0.2), canonical tenants (migration 0156), internal platform authority (PR #585/#586, 2026-07-29). The last full-journey validation predates every one of these changes.
findings.customer_impact: First client could hit a broken login, provisioning, or scan path live in the meeting.
findings.business_impact: A failed first engagement destroys local-market referral credibility that the go-to-market depends on.
findings.recommended_action: Repeat the full H1-H18 dry run against production infrastructure on the current stack, including named-user portal invite -> OIDC login -> engagement access, all 9+ scans, report generation, PDF export, portal remediation loop.
findings.minimum_fix: One complete production dry run with a written pass/fail log; fix blockers found.
findings.validation: Dry-run log committed to docs/operators/ with timestamps and outcomes for each H step.
findings.exit_criteria: All H1-H18 steps pass on production within 7 days of first client meeting.

findings.title: Portal named-user login is the only production login path and is unproven with a real client user
findings.evidence: apps/portal/app/api/auth/login/route.ts returns 403 PORTAL_DEMO_AUTH_DISABLED in any prod-like env (fail closed, isProdLikeEnv in apps/portal/lib/session.ts). The only remaining path is invite -> OIDC (apps/portal/app/api/auth/oidc/*, accept-invite) backed by portal_users (migration 0164). ROADMAP marks 'PR B: Portal Production Named-User Cutover' and 'PR C: logout revocation' as in progress (branches named), while the code for both is present on main - status ambiguity itself is a risk. Invite email delivery depends on RESEND_API_KEY (apps/console/lib/mailer.ts throws if unset).
findings.customer_impact: If OIDC/invite is misconfigured in prod, clients cannot access the portal at all - there is no fallback.
findings.business_impact: Portal is the primary deliverable surface; lockout means the engagement collapses to emailed PDFs.
findings.recommended_action: Provision a real external test user end-to-end in production: console invite -> Resend email -> accept-invite -> OIDC login -> engagement pages -> logout revocation. Confirm RESEND_API_KEY, Auth0 app config, and PORTAL_SESSION_SECRET in Vercel prod.
findings.minimum_fix: One successful external-identity portal session in production plus logout revocation check (portal_user_sessions row revoked).
findings.validation: Session created and revoked; core DELETE /portal/named-sessions/self returns success; documented in dry-run log.
findings.exit_criteria: External test user completes full portal journey in production.

findings.title: No documented or tested database backup and restore for production Postgres
findings.evidence: Zero backup/restore runbooks: grep across docs/operators/, deploy/, Makefile finds no pg_dump/restore procedure. The ops_governance subsystem (migration 0051, api/db_models.py OpsBackupRecord/OpsRestoreRecord) is a record-keeping ledger, not a backup mechanism. Production DB is Railway Postgres (CLIENT_READINESS A1/A7); Railway plan-level backup behavior is unverified. docs/ai/R1_AUTHORITY_AUDIT.md:119 previously flagged the filesystem tenant registry as having no backup.
findings.customer_impact: Evidence chains, findings, and reports for a paying client could be unrecoverable after a DB loss - directly contradicting the tamper-evident/audit-ready positioning.
findings.business_impact: The DPA (contracts/dpa_template.md) makes data-handling commitments the platform cannot currently evidence.
findings.recommended_action: Confirm Railway automated backups on the current plan (upgrade if Hobby lacks them), perform one restore into a scratch database, verify row counts and a known engagement, write docs/operators/backup_restore.md.
findings.minimum_fix: One verified restore + runbook.
findings.validation: Restore test log with checksums/row counts.
findings.exit_criteria: Documented, dated, successful restore test.

findings.title: Production runs on hobby-tier single-instance infrastructure with in-process background work
findings.evidence: CLIENT_READINESS A10 (Railway Hobby plan headroom) is unchecked; B1 notes Prometheus is not wired 'Hobby plan has no scrape endpoint'. Scans and AI report generation run via FastAPI BackgroundTasks in the API process (api/field_assessment.py lines 3421-3767; SYSTEM.md design decision 'No Celery/NATS overhead'). Durable scan jobs (services/field_assessment/durable_job_service.py, FaScanJob lease model, migration 0084) mitigate restart loss for scans but execution is still in-process.
findings.customer_impact: A memory/CPU ceiling or dyno restart mid-meeting kills a live scan or report generation in front of the client.
findings.business_impact: In-meeting failure is the highest-visibility failure mode for the assessor-led model.
findings.recommended_action: Verify or upgrade the Railway plan before first engagement; load-check one full scan suite + report generation concurrently; document restart/recovery semantics for in-flight jobs (orphan recovery exists - verify it fires).
findings.minimum_fix: Plan headroom confirmed with a concurrent scan+report load test; orphan-recovery observed once.
findings.validation: Load test notes + Railway metrics screenshot in dry-run log.
findings.exit_criteria: Full scan suite + report completes with >30% memory headroom.

findings.title: No incident response or deployment rollback runbook despite recent production incidents
findings.evidence: ROADMAP.md Platform Recovery series (R0 fail-closed provisioning hotfix #549, R0.1 error taxonomy, R0.2 'three production bugs ... found and fixed during live incident recovery', R1 authority audit, R3/R6/R7) documents real July incidents handled ad hoc. docs/operators/ contains no incident-response or rollback procedure; deploy is Railway GitHub auto-deploy (ROADMAP PR 39) with no documented rollback step.
findings.customer_impact: Outage during a paid engagement with no practiced recovery path extends downtime and damages trust.
findings.business_impact: Solo-operator model makes an unwritten process a single point of failure.
findings.recommended_action: Write a one-page incident runbook (detect via Sentry/UptimeRobot -> assess -> rollback via Railway redeploy of previous build -> client comms template) and a rollback drill: redeploy previous image once, timed.
findings.minimum_fix: Runbook + one timed rollback drill.
findings.validation: Rollback drill timing recorded.
findings.exit_criteria: Documented rollback completed in under 15 minutes.

findings.title: DPA promises 90-day retention but no purge mechanism exists
findings.evidence: contracts/dpa_template.md commits to 90-day retention; contracts/connectors/policies/fg_field_assessment.json sets retention.days=90. CLIENT_READINESS F7 explicitly open: 'no scheduled job or API endpoint purges engagement data after the window.' No purge implementation found in api/, services/, or jobs/ (grep purge/retention).
findings.customer_impact: Client data retained beyond the contractual window; a deletion request has no supported path.
findings.business_impact: Signed DPA becomes a liability the day the first engagement passes day 90.
findings.recommended_action: Before client one: manual purge runbook (SQL script per engagement, respecting evidence-lifecycle locks and legal holds) plus a calendar control. Before client 3-10: scheduled purge job honoring FaLegalHold.
findings.minimum_fix: Manual purge runbook + tested script on a dry-run engagement.
findings.validation: Dry-run engagement purged in staging; row counts verified.
findings.exit_criteria: Runbook exists and was executed once against test data.

findings.title: Console surface overload: 20+ nav items across 6 groups, four overlapping dashboards, legacy decision-engine pages
findings.evidence: packages/navigation/src/registrations/console.ts registers ~22 items: 4 dashboard-class pages (executive-intelligence, command-center, operations-center, control-tower) plus decision-engine-era pages (decisions, forensics, alignment, provenance, corpus, retrieval, ingestion, evaluation-lab, policies, providers) that are not part of field-assessment delivery. apps/console/app has 37 page.tsx files.
findings.customer_impact: Screen-share during engagements exposes half-relevant surfaces; operator navigation cost is high.
findings.business_impact: Longer operator ramp; higher chance of demo stumbles; enterprise viewers judge coherence.
findings.recommended_action: Launch mode: role/flag-gate the nav registry down to Field Assessments, Clients (tenants), Workforce Intelligence, Readiness, Keys, Settings, and ONE dashboard. Hide decision-engine/AI-plane legacy groups until those tiers sell.
findings.minimum_fix: Feature-flag nav gating in packages/navigation (visibility predicate already supports per-principal filtering via getNavigationItemsForPrincipal).
findings.validation: Operator completes engagement E2E using only visible nav.
findings.exit_criteria: Default operator sees <= 9 nav items.

findings.title: Portal ships visible stub/immature pages
findings.evidence: apps/portal/app/changes/page.tsx: `const [groups] = useState<ChangeGroup[]>([])` - groups can never be populated; the page permanently renders an empty state. apps/portal/app/export/page.tsx defaults all export options to available:false. Portal nav registers 12+ destinations (packages/navigation/src/registrations/portal.ts) for a client who needs ~6.
findings.customer_impact: A paying client clicking 'Changes' sees a dead page; erodes the professional-delivery impression.
findings.business_impact: Trust damage is disproportionate to the engineering saved.
findings.recommended_action: Hide /changes, and any export option that is not live, behind capability flags for launch. Trim default portal nav to: Dashboard, Assessment (engagement), Findings, Remediation, Reports, Support (+ Assistant when QA-approved).
findings.minimum_fix: Remove stub pages from nav registry; direct-URL access shows a friendly 'coming soon' with support link.
findings.validation: Click-through of every visible portal nav item shows real data on a dry-run engagement.
findings.exit_criteria: No visible portal page renders a permanent empty/unavailable state.

findings.title: Authoritative docs materially contradict the implementation
findings.evidence: SYSTEM.md v1.2 (2026-06-02) claims assessment endpoints are 'no auth required' - api/assessments.py now requires the ingest:assessment scope and lead-namespace tenant binding. SYSTEM.md says 77 migrations - there are 168. SYSTEM.md says 'SET LOCAL for tenant context uses f-string' - api/db.py:1911 uses parameterized set_config. CLIENT_READINESS.md H1-H18 unchecked vs ROADMAP row 32 claiming done. STATUS.md shows 'Alignment 27%' template noise.
findings.customer_impact: Indirect - but an enterprise security review reading SYSTEM.md would conclude assessment endpoints are unauthenticated.
findings.business_impact: Docs are the sales-engineering surface for enterprise deals; stale claims are worse than absent ones.
findings.recommended_action: One reconciliation pass: SYSTEM.md v1.3 (auth model, migration count, tenant-context mechanism, current app inventory), CLIENT_READINESS refresh with dated dry-run state, delete or regenerate STATUS.md.
findings.minimum_fix: Correct the three security-relevant SYSTEM.md claims and re-date CLIENT_READINESS.
findings.validation: Doc claims spot-checked against code.
findings.exit_criteria: SYSTEM.md security claims match implementation.

findings.title: Alerting exists but alert response ownership and triage are undefined
findings.evidence: Sentry DSN confirmed capturing (CLIENT_READINESS B3); UptimeRobot on 3 services (A9/B2); Prometheus /metrics exists (api/main.py:870) but is unscraped in prod (B1). No document maps alert -> action -> owner; docs/operators/ has no on-call or triage note.
findings.customer_impact: Client-facing outage may go unnoticed until the client reports it.
findings.business_impact: Support expectations in engagement letters are uncovered.
findings.recommended_action: Half-day doc: which alerts page the operator (UptimeRobot down, Sentry error spike), response-time expectation, and the first three diagnostic steps per alert class.
findings.minimum_fix: One-page alert triage doc; Sentry alert rule for new-issue notifications to email/phone.
findings.validation: Test alert fired and acknowledged within target.
findings.exit_criteria: Documented triage path for both alert sources.

findings.title: Report and PDF quality needs a human QA pass on real engagement data
findings.evidence: PDF export implemented (services/governance/report/serialization.py export_pdf_bytes, reportlab in requirements.txt; ROADMAP PR 38 with cover/exec summary/findings/appendix). Language rules enforced in the legacy assessment reports engine (api/reports_engine.py per SYSTEM.md). Report quality scores wired to real evidence (TC-7 #540). What is unverified: current-stack PDF rendering quality, executive summary tone, and advisory-language consistency across the FA report path - last human-validated at the 2026-06-01 dry run.
findings.customer_impact: The PDF is the artifact the buyer forwards to their board; a blank section or robotic exec summary undercuts the fee.
findings.business_impact: Report quality is the conversion lever for tier upsell (FOUNDER_DIRECTIVE: 'legally defensible' report standard).
findings.recommended_action: During the dry run, review every PDF section against a checklist (no placeholders, advisory language, manifest hash present, data-collected appendix populated) and fix defects.
findings.minimum_fix: QA checklist executed once on dry-run PDF; defects fixed.
findings.validation: Signed-off checklist stored with the dry-run log.
findings.exit_criteria: Dry-run PDF passes checklist.

findings.title: No secret rotation procedure; production secrets set ad hoc during incidents
findings.evidence: At least 12 production secrets across Railway/Vercel (CLIENT_READINESS A4-A6: FG_KEY_PEPPER, FG_SIGNING_SECRET, FG_INTERNAL_AUTH_SECRET, FG_REPORT_SIGNING_KEY, PORTAL_SESSION_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, Auth0, Stripe, Anthropic...). env/prod.env in-repo contains placeholders only (verified - no live values). R6 gateway secret convergence (#553) unified resolution order but no rotation runbook exists; some secrets were handled during July incident recovery.
findings.customer_impact: Indirect until a leak; then recovery is improvised.
findings.business_impact: Enterprise questionnaires ask for rotation policy; 'none' costs deals.
findings.recommended_action: Inventory secrets (name, location, blast radius, rotation steps) in docs/operators/secret_rotation.md; rotate anything that was pasted into chats/tickets during July incidents.
findings.minimum_fix: Inventory + rotation steps for the 5 highest-blast-radius secrets.
findings.validation: One low-risk secret rotated successfully following the doc.
findings.exit_criteria: Rotation doc exists; suspect secrets rotated.

findings.title: Anthropic API funding is trivially low for a paid engagement cadence
findings.evidence: CLIENT_READINESS B4 (2026-05-31): $3.50 balance, ~$0.05-0.25 per engagement. Two months of merged AI-touching features (executive summary, explainer, entity extraction, portal assistant) have run since; current balance unverified.
findings.customer_impact: Report generation fails mid-engagement with a billing error.
findings.business_impact: Embarrassing, trivially preventable failure.
findings.recommended_action: Enable auto-recharge with a monthly cap; add balance check to first_client_prep.md pre-flight.
findings.minimum_fix: Auto-recharge enabled.
findings.validation: Console shows auto-recharge on.
findings.exit_criteria: Auto-recharge configured.

findings.title: No client email notifications, scheduled re-scans, or before/after posture deltas
findings.evidence: CLIENT_READINESS G5-G8 all open. Portal notifications page derives in-app items from audit events only (apps/portal/app/notifications/page.tsx); no email nudges (Resend is wired for invites only, apps/console/app/api/email/route.ts). Drift detection exists (PR 6) but is not surfaced as a client-facing delta; /changes page is a stub.
findings.customer_impact: Clients disengage between report delivery and follow-up; remediation stalls silently.
findings.business_impact: Weakens the remediation-loop moat and the continuous-governance upsell that the strategy depends on.
findings.recommended_action: After client 1: weekly digest email (open findings, overdue remediations) reusing the Resend path; 30-day re-scan runbook (manual trigger is supported today); snapshot delta view feeding the /changes page.
findings.minimum_fix: Manual: operator calendar reminder + templated 30-day follow-up email (letters/5 exists).
findings.validation: One client receives digest; re-scan compares to baseline.
findings.exit_criteria: Automated digest + documented re-scan before client 10.

findings.title: api/field_assessment.py is a 12,747-line single module
findings.evidence: wc -l api/field_assessment.py = 12747; 63 route handlers, 98 require_permission call sites in one file. Route/permission drift risk is currently contained by CI gates (AuditCoverageValidator, capability sprawl guard) but review cost per change is high.
findings.customer_impact: Indirect: slower, riskier fixes during live engagements.
findings.business_impact: Engineering velocity tax on the core product surface.
findings.recommended_action: Post-launch: split by resource (engagements, scans, findings, reports, questionnaires, governance) preserving route paths; no behavior change.
findings.minimum_fix: None pre-launch. Do not refactor during the launch window.
findings.validation: Contract diff empty (openapi.json unchanged) after split.
findings.exit_criteria: No file over 3k lines in api/ for FA.

findings.title: In-memory state in BFF and explainer breaks under multi-instance scaling
findings.evidence: apps/portal/app/api/auth/login/route.ts uses an in-process Map for login rate limiting (mitigated: route is prod-disabled); finding-explainer LRU cache is in-memory (ROADMAP P2 item 12 open); portal core-proxy rate limiter has Redis with in-memory fallback (ROADMAP item 18 done). Single-instance deployment makes this acceptable today.
findings.customer_impact: None at current scale; cache misses and rate-limit inconsistency if scaled out.
findings.business_impact: Blocks horizontal scaling at client ~10+.
findings.recommended_action: Before scaling past one API instance: Redis-backed explainer cache; audit remaining in-memory maps.
findings.minimum_fix: None pre-launch; document single-instance assumption in ops notes.
findings.validation: Two-instance staging run with consistent behavior.
findings.exit_criteria: No correctness-relevant in-memory state at 2+ instances.

findings.title: Metrics exist but are unscraped; no SLOs or dashboards in production
findings.evidence: api/main.py:870 exposes /metrics (prometheus_client); many subsystems emit counters (trust enforcement, subscriptions, capability checks). CLIENT_READINESS B1: not wired in prod. deploy/grafana + deploy/prometheus exist for local compose only.
findings.customer_impact: Slow detection of degradation that Sentry/UptimeRobot do not catch (latency, queue depth).
findings.business_impact: SLA conversations at client ~10 require this.
findings.recommended_action: Stage 3: hosted scrape (Grafana Cloud free tier) of /metrics; one dashboard: request rate/latency/error, scan job states, report generation duration; 3 SLOs.
findings.minimum_fix: None pre-launch (Sentry+UptimeRobot suffice for stage 1-2).
findings.validation: Dashboard shows live prod data.
findings.exit_criteria: 3 SLOs defined and graphed.

findings.title: Repository hygiene: committed runtime artifacts, duplicate app trees, root-level doc sprawl
findings.evidence: frostgate_decisions.db-shm (SQLite shared-memory file) committed at repo root; legacy top-level trees (console/ referenced by SYSTEM.md, ui/, main/, backend/, admin_gateway/) alongside apps/*; ~25 planning/audit .md files at root (ALIGNMENT_AUDIT, AUDIT_TRACKER, POST_PT_AUDIT, H14_RBAC_GAP_REPORT, frostgate_tree_everything.txt...).
findings.customer_impact: None direct.
findings.business_impact: Due-diligence reviewers see clutter; new engineers lose time.
findings.recommended_action: Post-launch sweep: remove runtime artifacts from git, archive stale root docs into docs/archive/, delete or clearly mark dead app trees.
findings.minimum_fix: Remove db-shm artifact from git.
findings.validation: git ls-files clean of runtime artifacts.
findings.exit_criteria: Root directory contains only live entry points and the 6 authoritative docs.

findings.title: admin_gateway production role is ambiguous
findings.evidence: admin_gateway/ is a separate FastAPI service in docker-compose.yml:319 and is the target of the Identity Foundation PR series (invitation start-auth, OIDC session issuance). Production topology per CLIENT_READINESS is Railway API + Vercel console/portal with BFFs calling core directly (CORE_API_URL); no Railway service for admin_gateway is documented. Whether identity-governance flows that assume the gateway are exercised in prod is unresolved.
findings.customer_impact: Features tested against a topology that production does not run.
findings.business_impact: Wasted investment or silent prod gaps in the identity control plane.
findings.recommended_action: Decide: deploy admin_gateway in prod, or declare BFF->core the production identity path and mark gateway-only flows as non-prod. Document in SYSTEM.md.
findings.minimum_fix: One-paragraph topology decision in SYSTEM.md v1.3.
findings.validation: SYSTEM.md states the prod identity path; dry run exercises it.
findings.exit_criteria: Documented topology matches production.

findings.title: Continuous governance is the recurring-revenue engine and has no offer - launch a zero-engineering CG v0, automate by client 10
findings.evidence: Engagement status machine includes 'monitoring' (migration 0073); governance_orchestration exists (13 trigger types) but no scheduler execution; no client-facing CG offer. Every CG v0 step already runs manually on shipped features: baseline = delivered report + verification bundle (0086); monthly drift = re-run scan suite on same engagement + templated delta email; quarterly review = regenerated report version; risk trend = snapshot history (PR 37); renewal anchored by the day-90 DPA retention decision (FG-LR-006).
findings.customer_impact: Client has no visible path from report to ongoing governance; the one-time report ages without a stay-accurate offer.
findings.business_impact: CG converts customer-acquisition engagements into recurring revenue (a single CG client at $750-1500/mo out-earns the assessment that acquired them) and starts the longitudinal drift history - the non-backfillable moat asset. Deferring the OFFER (vs the scheduler) forfeits both.
findings.recommended_action: Launch: CG v0 as a founder-delivered manual service (0 engineering days) pitched at every report delivery - baseline / monthly drift check / quarterly review / renewal. Stage 3: automate via FG-LR-014 (digests, scheduled re-scans) and turn the /changes stub into the client delta view. Full design in CUSTOMER_COMMERCIAL_READINESS.md CG section.
findings.minimum_fix: CG v0 one-pager (offer, cadence, price) in the engagement paper; pitch at first report delivery.
findings.validation: CG v0 offered to design partner at delivery; one monthly drift cycle executed manually.
findings.exit_criteria: >=1 client on CG v0 before Stage 2 exit; automation replacing manual steps before client 10.

findings.title: Enterprise key-management stub providers: stop pre-launch investment
findings.evidence: ROADMAP PR 17.7C: 6 enterprise stub providers (AWS KMS, Azure KV, Google KMS, Vault, PKCS#11, HSM) all health()=NOT_IMPLEMENTED, sign/verify raise NotImplementedError; 256 tests over stubs.
findings.customer_impact: None - no first-10 client needs HSM-backed signing.
findings.business_impact: Engineering time diverted from launch-critical work.
findings.recommended_action: Freeze. Revisit at the first enterprise deal that names KMS in security requirements.
findings.minimum_fix: N/A - defer.
findings.validation: N/A
findings.exit_criteria: No further PRs in this area before client 10.

findings.title: Subscription/billing v2 capability machinery: defer completion, invoice manually
findings.evidence: ROADMAP P1.2-P1.5 (policy bundles, capability enforcement, subscription engine, billing integration) are open PRs with placeholder 'PR PR_NUMBER' identifiers. Stripe webhook exists. First engagements at $299-$999 to $15k are invoice-priced services, not metered SaaS.
findings.customer_impact: None - clients receive invoices either way.
findings.business_impact: Completing metering before revenue exists is inverted priority.
findings.recommended_action: Manual invoicing (Stripe invoice or bank transfer) through client 10. Land the open capability PRs only if they gate portal features already in use; otherwise park.
findings.minimum_fix: N/A - defer.
findings.validation: N/A
findings.exit_criteria: First 3 clients invoiced manually without friction.

findings.title: Legacy Tier-1 self-serve assessment funnel: hide for launch
findings.evidence: apps/console/app/{page,onboarding,assessment}.tsx (landing, wizard) target the self-serve $299 Snapshot motion; api/assessments.py includes a checkout endpoint. The actual launch motion is assessor-led field assessment. Two funnels create split focus and an untested paid path.
findings.customer_impact: A stranger buying the self-serve product hits an unstaffed support path.
findings.business_impact: Unattended paid product carries brand risk with zero pipeline behind it.
findings.recommended_action: Hide/park the self-serve funnel and Stripe checkout for launch; apps/web is the marketing surface. Revive self-serve when there is capacity to support it.
findings.minimum_fix: Remove public links to onboarding/assessment wizard; leave code in place.
findings.validation: No public path to checkout.
findings.exit_criteria: Self-serve unreachable without a direct URL.

findings.title: Trust-layer expansion (open provenance/replay PRs) - freeze at current depth
findings.evidence: Evidence provenance arc PRs 1.1-1.5A, trust graph 1.6+, replay 1.10 planned; several still open per ROADMAP. What is already merged (Ed25519 signing, verification bundles migration 0086, transparency ledger, evidence lifecycle locks migration 0083, append-only triggers) is more cryptographic depth than any first-10 client will evaluate.
findings.customer_impact: None incremental.
findings.business_impact: Every trust-layer day pre-launch is a day not spent on the dry run, UX gating, or ops gaps.
findings.recommended_action: Land or close open PRs to stop WIP drift, then freeze the arc until a client or regulator asks for replay proofs. The moat now compounds through usage (engagements), not more layers.
findings.minimum_fix: N/A - defer.
findings.validation: N/A
findings.exit_criteria: No new trust-layer PRs before client 3.

findings.title: Legacy /remediation API deprecated but still mounted
findings.evidence: ROADMAP R-1 (#543): api/remediation_authority.py declared canonical; all 17 routes in api/remediation.py marked deprecated but still served.
findings.customer_impact: None if portal uses the canonical path (R-2 #545 wired RemediationCenter to canonical).
findings.business_impact: Duplicate state risk if anything still writes the legacy path.
findings.recommended_action: Post-launch: verify zero traffic to /remediation/* then remove.
findings.minimum_fix: N/A - defer.
findings.validation: Access logs show no legacy hits for 30 days.
findings.exit_criteria: Legacy router removed.

findings.title: Executive report lacks business-risk and financial-impact chapters and a Top-10 actions page
findings.evidence: Current PDF (PR 38): cover, AI exec summary, confidence, findings, remediation plan, framework coverage, evidence appendix + disclosure - a strong assessor's report. Missing for the enterprise buyer's spine: business-risk narrative conditioned on industry (playbook sector data exists to drive it), financial-impact exposure ranges (must be cited-benchmark ranges with methodology note - fabricated precision would violate the legally-defensible standard), and a one-page ranked Top-10 actions (data exists in portal immediate-actions/quick-wins but is not distilled into the PDF).
findings.customer_impact: CISO cannot hand the report upward without translation; board sees findings, not business meaning.
findings.business_impact: The report is the artifact that sells the next engagement up the buyer's chain; without chapters 2-4 it caps at the technical buyer.
findings.recommended_action: Report v2: add Business Risk (prompt+template work on sector data), Financial Impact (cited ranges + methodology note, advisory-labeled), Top-10 Actions page (serialization of existing quick-wins data). Spec in CUSTOMER_COMMERCIAL_READINESS.md.
findings.minimum_fix: Top-10 Actions page alone (pure serialization) if time-constrained.
findings.validation: Report v2 reviewed against the chapter spec on a real engagement; financial-impact methodology reviewed before first client-facing use.
findings.exit_criteria: Stage 2 clients receive the v2 spine.

findings.title: Console lacks an Operator Home work-queue view - operators navigate by memory, not by queue
findings.evidence: Four dashboard-class pages exist but none answers 'what needs my attention now'. All seven required queues are backed by existing data: today's engagements (fa_engagements), waiting-on-client (invitations, audit-event recency, next_attestation_due), evidence needing review (lifecycle collected state, provenance review), reports pending QA (report versions + gate), high-risk findings, governance alerts (fired-alerts log PR 37, drift PR 6), system health (GET /scan-jobs dead-letter, startup validation). Design in CONSOLE_UX_AUDIT.md section 5.
findings.customer_impact: Indirect: slower operator response to client-facing queues (QA, evidence review, stalled remediation).
findings.business_impact: Queue-driven console is the precondition for a second operator being productive - the Stage 4 transferability gate.
findings.recommended_action: Operator Home v1: single screen, 7 collapsible queues with counts, click lands on the action. Replaces the interim dashboard after launch.
findings.minimum_fix: Launch uses interim /dashboard (FG-LR-007 gating); Operator Home is the Stage 2-3 replacement.
findings.validation: Operator clears a full day's work from Home without using primary nav.
findings.exit_criteria: Home replaces dashboard before the second operator onboards; failed-scan queue visible.

findings.title: Portal lacks a continuous-journey model - clients navigate pages instead of being carried through steps
findings.evidence: All journey steps exist as pages (login, engagement, documents, findings, reports, remediation) but nothing sequences them. Design in PORTAL_UX_AUDIT.md section 5: BFF-computed journeyState from existing endpoints drives a persistent stepper + single next-action card. Includes the minute-five confidence fix: dashboard hero should lead with 2-3 concrete plain-language discoveries about the client's own environment (scan data already produces them) before abstract charts.
findings.customer_impact: Client must infer their next action; the worth-paying-for moment (minute five) currently leans on abstract charts instead of concrete discoveries.
findings.business_impact: Journey confidence drives remediation engagement, renewal, and referrals - the segment's whole growth loop.
findings.recommended_action: Stage 2-3: journey shell (stepper + next-action engine, ~2 days) on existing pages. Launch: fold the discoveries-first dashboard reorder (~0.5 day) into FG-LR-008.
findings.minimum_fix: Discoveries-first dashboard hero at launch (inside FG-LR-008); stepper post-launch.
findings.validation: Design partner completes evidence upload and remediation start without operator navigation help.
findings.exit_criteria: Stage 2 clients see the stepper; zero navigation-confusion support calls in a full engagement.
